name: MA-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's 11-point Democratic lean in a strongly blue state
Auchincloss's large financial advantage ($7.3M cash vs. ~$1K)
Incumbency and Polymarket pricing the Democrat at ~97%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly Democratic: an 11-point partisan lean, an incumbent with a massive cash advantage, and prediction markets pricing the Democrat near 97%. With no competitive polling or outside spending against the incumbent, there is no evidence to move off the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: A surprise primary upset or a late redistricting change would be the main ways this race becomes competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jake Auchincloss seeks another term in a Massachusetts district that leans Democratic by about 11 points. He enters the general election with a large financial edge, holding roughly $7.3 million on hand after raising over $3.6 million, while Republican Thomas Stalcup has raised only about $26,000 and has minimal cash remaining. No outside groups are spending against the incumbent.

No public general-election polling covers the race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets price the Democratic side at roughly 97 percent. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and fundraising disparity makes this a Safe Democratic seat, with the main uncertainty coming from turnout variation rather than any measurable challenger strength.
